title: Recording: Hi, Hi, Hi by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Alan Parsons

Wings continued work on ‘Hi, Hi, Hi’ on 24 September 1972.

They had recorded a satisfactory backing track, take 61, on 20 September. However, upon reviewing the many attempts, engineer Alan Parsons suggested they revert instead to a live version recorded in Groningen in the Netherlands during the Wings Over Europe Tour.

It was a lot of takes. He was just looking for some feel they were never gonna get. It was so much better live. The live version was very different. I preferred it, and I told him so.
Alan Parsons
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 1: 1969-73

Paul McCartney disagreed, and work continued on studio take 61. Parsons needed to create a reduction mix to free up space on the multitrack tape, after which Denny Laine and Henry McCullough added three slide guitar parts, and McCartney re-recorded his two lead vocals tracks.

The session ended early, and 5.45 Wings left Abbey Road to celebrate Linda McCartney’s 31s birthday at 7 Cavendish Avenue.

Page last updated: 24 November 2025
